cover: Before you go headless with WordPress

slides.title: Your editors like WordPress
slides.body: They’re comfortable in it and you don’t want to retrain them. If editing’s the main complaint, look at leaving instead.

slides.title: The complaints come from visitors
slides.body: Slow pages and outages for visitors, more than plugin updates nobody trusts and upkeep that eats into the week.

slides.title: Visitors mostly read pages
slides.body: No shopping carts or logged-in areas that need WordPress running for each visitor.

slides.title: A minute or two to go live is fine
slides.body: Edits appear after a rebuild. At a clinic we worked with, a plugin waits ninety seconds so ten quick saves become one rebuild.

slides.title: Ask the builder: how strict is the build?
slides.body: A renamed field should stop it with a clear error. Missing content should never get filled with placeholder text.

slides.title: Ask to see a failed build
slides.body: The previous site should stay up. Find out how editors will notice the failure and who helps them publish again.
